capabilities.title: GPU sizing for vLLM by model scale
capabilities.summary: Hardware requirements table: which GPU count/class serves which model size, and when quantization becomes mandatory.

when: Sizing GPUs for a planned vLLM deployment.
Checking whether a model fits the available GPUs before serving it.

steps: 7B-13B models: 1x A10 (24GB) or A100 (40GB).
30B-40B models: 2x A100 (40GB) with tensor parallelism.
70B+ models: 4x A100 (40GB) or 2x A100 (80GB); use AWQ/GPTQ quantization.
Platforms: NVIDIA (primary), AMD ROCm, Intel GPUs, TPUs.

capabilities.title: Deploy a production OpenAI-compatible vLLM endpoint with monitoring
capabilities.summary: Configure vllm serve by model size, load-test, enable Prometheus metrics, deploy via Docker, and verify latency/throughput targets.

when: Deploying a production LLM API (100+ req/sec).
Serving OpenAI-compatible endpoints for multi-user applications (chatbots, assistants).
Low latency with high throughput is required from a persistent service.
avoid_when: CPU/edge or single-user inference — use llama.cpp.
Research, prototyping, or one-off generation — use HuggingFace transformers.
Already committed to the HuggingFace serving ecosystem — consider Text-Generation-Inference.
One-shot processing of a fixed dataset — use offline batch inference instead of a server.

steps: Configure server flags by model size: 7B-13B single GPU with --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 8192; 30B-70B add --tensor-parallel-size 4 and --quantization awq; production adds --enable-prefix-caching --enable-metrics --metrics-port 9090 --host 0.0.0.0.
Load-test with limited traffic before production (locust) and check latency/throughput targets.
Enable monitoring: scrape Prometheus metrics on :9090 — vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds, vllm:num_requests_running, vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc.
Deploy via Docker (vllm/vllm-openai image, --gpus all, port 8000) for consistent environments.
Verify performance: TTFT < 500ms for short prompts, throughput above target, GPU utilization > 80%, no OOM errors in logs.

validation: TTFT (time to first token) < 500ms for short prompts.
vllm:* Prometheus metrics are scrapeable on the metrics port.
recovery: OOM during model loading: lower --gpu-memory-utilization to 0.7 and --max-model-len to 4096, or serve a quantized model (--quantization awq).
Slow first token (TTFT > 1s): --enable-prefix-caching for repeated prompts; --enable-chunked-prefill for long prompts.
Low throughput (<50 req/sec): raise --max-num-seqs to 512 and confirm GPU utilization > 80% via nvidia-smi.
Model not found: add --trust-remote-code for custom models.
Slower than expected with tensor parallelism: --tensor-parallel-size must be a power of 2.

capabilities.title: Offline batch inference without a server
capabilities.summary: Run the LLM engine in-process over a full prompt list in one generate call — vLLM batches internally; no server, no manual chunking.

when: Processing a large set of prompts offline (dataset scoring, generation for evaluation).
Batch generation inside a pipeline where a persistent server adds needless overhead.
avoid_when: A persistent multi-user endpoint is needed — use the production deployment workflow.
CPU-only or single-prompt interactive use — use llama.cpp or HuggingFace transformers.

steps: Load all prompts into a list.
Construct the engine once: LLM(model=..., tensor_parallel_size=N, gpu_memory_utilization=0.9, max_model_len=...).
Define SamplingParams(temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop=[...]).
Pass the FULL prompt list to a single llm.generate(prompts, sampling) call — vLLM handles batching internally; do not chunk manually.
Extract output.outputs[0].text (and token counts) per result and write JSONL.

validation: One generated output per input prompt (results length equals prompts length).
No manual chunking loop wraps llm.generate.
recovery: OOM: lower gpu_memory_utilization and/or max_model_len, or use a quantized model.

capabilities.title: Serve a quantized model when the full-precision model exceeds VRAM
capabilities.summary: Pick AWQ/GPTQ/FP8, use a pre-quantized checkpoint, launch with --quantization, and verify accuracy against the unquantized baseline.

when: The full-precision model does not fit available GPU memory (e.g., 70B-class on limited VRAM).
A larger model is needed on fewer/smaller GPUs.
avoid_when: The model already fits comfortably unquantized — quantization adds an accuracy-verification burden without a memory need.

expected_outcomes: A 70B-class model serves in ~40GB VRAM with AWQ.

steps: Choose the method: AWQ (best for 70B, minimal accuracy loss), GPTQ (widest model support), FP8 (fastest on H100).
Use a pre-quantized checkpoint from HuggingFace (e.g., TheBloke/*-AWQ) rather than quantizing yourself.
Launch: vllm serve <quantized-model> --quantization awq --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 (tensor-parallel as needed).
Verify accuracy: compare quantized vs non-quantized responses on task-representative samples.

validation: The model loads within available VRAM.
Task-specific output quality is comparable to the non-quantized baseline on sampled prompts.
recovery: Still OOM: lower --gpu-memory-utilization / --max-model-len or increase tensor parallelism.

capabilities.title: Triage an underperforming vLLM endpoint
capabilities.summary: Read-only checks — Prometheus metrics, GPU utilization, logs — that localize latency/throughput problems to a known remediation lever.

when: A running vLLM endpoint underperforms (TTFT > 1s or throughput < 50 req/sec) or errors under load.

steps: Scrape :9090/metrics and read vllm:time_to_first_token_seconds (latency), vllm:num_requests_running (load), vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc (KV-cache pressure).
Check GPU utilization with nvidia-smi — should be > 80% under load.
Check server logs for OOM errors.
Map symptom to lever: slow TTFT -> prefix caching / chunked prefill; low throughput -> --max-num-seqs, tensor-parallel power-of-2; slow generation -> speculative decoding (--speculative-model).
